Question Choices: Select which you would measure in meters: ~~eraser | building | finger | book~~
Solution: A building is large, so meters are a sensible unit. An eraser, finger and book are much smaller and are usually measured in centimeters.

Question Choices: Select which unit would probably be used to measure how long the gymnasium is?: ~~Centimeters | Meters~~
Solution: A gymnasium is many large steps long. Meters give a convenient measurement; centimeters would give a very large count.

Question Choices: Select which unit would probably be used to measure how long a classroom door is?: ~~Inches | Feet~~
Solution: A classroom door is several feet long. Feet are a more convenient unit than inches for this length.

Question Choices: Select which you would measure in centimeters: ~~pencil | tree | building | basketball-court~~
Solution: A pencil is a small object whose length is conveniently measured in centimeters. The other choices are much larger.

Question Choices: Select which is closest to how long a necklace is: ~~40-centimeters | 40-meters~~
Solution: A necklace fits around a neck. Forty centimeters is reasonable; forty meters is far too long. Select 40-centimeters.

Question Choices: Select which is closest to how long a car is: ~~5-centimeters | 5-meters~~
Solution: A car is several meters long. Five centimeters would be smaller than a hand. Select 5-meters.

Question Choices: Select which you would measure in inches: ~~smartphone-screen | door | football-field~~
Solution: A smartphone screen is a small object, so inches are convenient. A door or football field is much larger.

Question Choices: Select which you would measure in feet: ~~paperclip | fishing-rod | eraser | laptop-screen~~
Solution: A fishing rod is several feet long. The other listed objects are small enough to measure conveniently in inches.

Question Choices: Select which is closest to how tall a telephone pole is?: ~~30-feet | 30-inches~~
Solution: A telephone pole is much taller than a person. Thirty feet is reasonable; thirty inches is only two and a half feet.

Question Choices: Select which is closest to how tall a postage stamp is: ~~1-feet | 1-inch~~
Solution: A postage stamp is small. One inch is reasonable; one foot would be much too tall.
